events.title: Kiel Canal Opens
events.description: German Emperor Wilhelm II formally opened the Kiel Canal. It cut across the base of the Jutland peninsula and linked the North Sea with the Baltic Sea.
events.significance: The canal spared ships the long trip around Denmark and became one of the busiest artificial waterways in the world. It also boosted Germany's naval and commercial strength.

events.title: Birth of Jean-Paul Sartre
events.description: The French philosopher, novelist and playwright was born in Paris. He grew up to be a leading voice of existentialism.
events.significance: Sartre's ideas about freedom and responsibility shaped postwar thought, literature and politics well beyond France.

events.title: Montini Becomes Pope Paul VI
events.description: Cardinal Giovanni Battista Montini was elected pope after the death of John XXIII. He took the name Paul VI.
events.significance: Paul VI oversaw the completion of the Second Vatican Council and its reforms, which reshaped modern Catholic worship and the Church's place in the world.

events.title: Death of Sukarno
events.description: Sukarno, the first President of Indonesia, died. He had led the country's independence movement and then spent years in political isolation.
events.significance: Sukarno was the central figure in Indonesia's emergence from Dutch colonial rule, and his legacy still shapes the country's national identity.

events.title: SpaceShipOne Makes the First Private Crewed Spaceflight
events.description: The privately funded SpaceShipOne climbed to just over 100 kilometers (62 miles), the commonly accepted boundary of space.
events.significance: The flight showed that spaceflight was no longer limited to government agencies. It helped launch the commercial space industry.
